subtitle: A pensioned prince, a frightened empire, and a poem that would not die

panels.shot: wide, low-angle twilight tableau facing a British cannon in a parade ground, with Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah standing calm before it, silhouettes of sepoys and colonial buildings behind
panels.action: Shankar Shah & Raghunath Shah stand bound yet upright before a looming British cannon in the Jabalpur parade ground at dusk, the outline of barracks and sepoy ranks hazy in the dusty light.

dialogue.text: Jabalpur, 18 September 1857: a pensioned Gond prince and his son are tied to British guns, and the empire trembles not at their swords, but at their songs.

i18n.hi: जबलपुर, १८ सितम्बर १८५७: पेंशनख़ोर गोंड राजकुमार और उसका बेटा अंग्रेज़ी तोपों से बाँधे गए, और साम्राज्य उनकी तलवारों से नहीं, उनके गीतों से काँप उठा।

panels.shot: slow push-in on an elderly Shankar Shah seated on a low cot in a modest house, maps and faded palm-leaf records of Garha-Katanga evoked in the background
panels.action: An aged Shankar Shah sits cross-legged on a rough cot in a simple Jabalpur dwelling, his gaze distant as if seeing, beyond the mud walls, the lost forests and forts of Garha-Katanga.

dialogue.text: He was no longer a ruling raja, only a pensioner of the Company, but Shankar Shah carried in his bones the memory of Garha-Katanga, of Gond kings who once held these forests and rivers.

i18n.hi: राज नहीं बचा था, बस कंपनी का पेंशनभोगी था, पर शंकर शाह की हड्डियों में गरहा‑कटँगाँ की, उन गोंड राजाओं की याद जगी थी जो कभी इन जंगलों‑नदियों के मालिक थे।

panels.shot: sweeping bird's-eye over a stylised map morphing across time from the Gond kingdom to Maratha and then British control
panels.action: A painted map scene shifts in vignettes: Gond forts at Garha and Mandla, Maratha horsemen sweeping in from the west, then British redcoat blocks overlaying the land around Jabalpur.

dialogue.text: A century earlier, Maratha raids in 1742 cracked that kingdom; Narhar Shah was seized, tortured and killed in 1781, and by 1817 Bhonsles and Britons shared and then claimed the Gond lands.

i18n.hi: एक सदी पहले, १७४२ की मराठा लूट ने रियासत तोड़ी; नहरार शाह को १७८१ में पकड़ा, यातना दी और मार डाला, और १८१७ तक भोंसले और अंग्रेज़ गोंड ज़मीन बाँटकर खुद के नाम कर गए।

panels.shot: medium shot of Shankar Shah walking slowly through a bazaar, with British officials and sepoys in the distance, his son Raghunath just behind him
panels.action: Shankar Shah walks with a staff through a dusty Jabalpur bazaar, Raghunath Shah at his side, as British officers on horseback and sepoys in neat lines move past in the background.

dialogue.text: Now, under British rule, he lived on a stipend, an old name in a new town of barracks and bungalows, his son Raghunath at his heel, and the Gond past reduced to a whisper.

i18n.hi: अब अंग्रेज़ी राज में वह वज़ीफ़ा लेकर जीता, बारहसिंहा सा बूढ़ा नाम, छावनियों‑बँगलों के नए कस्बे में, पीछे‑पीछे बेटा रघुनाथ, और गोंड अतीत बस हल्की फुसफुसाहट।

panels.shot: intimate interior medium shot, Shankar reciting to a small circle at night, Raghunath listening; a lamp flickers between them
panels.action: By the light of a single oil lamp, Shankar Shah raises his hand as he recites, while Raghunath Shah leans forward, listening, a few local men sitting in a half-circle in the dim interior.

dialogue.text: Local memory would later say he still made the past speak, in songs and poems that praised the land and its people, and prayed for deliverance from foreign rule.

i18n.hi: बाद की लोककथाएँ कहती हैं, वह अतीत को आज भी गाता था, गीतों‑कविताओं में धरती और लोगों की स्तुति, और परायी हुकूमत से मुक्ति की दुआ।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Jabalpur cantonment with drills; a translucent overlay suggests lines of text spreading like whispers
panels.action: Sepoys of the 52nd Bengal Native Infantry drill in straight ranks on the Jabalpur cantonment ground as faint lines of script seem to float outwards, hinting at rumours and verses moving through the air.

dialogue.text: In 1857, when cartridges and chapatis carried rumour faster than official letters, words were watched as closely as weapons. The British feared not just mutiny of arms, but contagion of ideas.

i18n.hi: १८५७ में, जब कारतूस और चपाती अफ़वाहें चिट्ठियों से तेज़ दौड़ाती थीं, शब्द भी हथियारों जितने ही निगरानी में थे। अंग्रेज़ों को डर था केवल हथियारों की बग़ावत का नहीं, ख़यालों के फैलाव का भी।

panels.shot: close-up on a British officer's desk with intercepted papers and a quill, the officer's hand hovering tensely
panels.action: A British officer's hand hovers over a bundle of crumpled papers on a desk in the Jabalpur station, the quill on his blotter stained and official seals lying open beside them.

dialogue.text: Colonial records from Jubbulpore speak of intercepted poems and suspicious gatherings, of verses they believed urged sepoys and villagers against Europeans and the Company.

i18n.hi: जबलपुर के उपनिवेशी अभिलेख रोकी गई कविताओं और संदिग्ध बैठकों का ज़िक्र करते हैं, उन पंक्तियों का, जिन्हें वे सिपाहियों और देहात को फ़िरंगी और कंपनी के ख़िलाफ़ भड़काता मानते थे।

panels.shot: dramatic low-angle as British sepoys and an officer arrive at Shankar’s house doorway, Shankar and Raghunath framed inside
panels.action: British sepoys with fixed bayonets and a stern officer darken the doorway of Shankar Shah's modest house, as Shankar and Raghunath stand within, surprised yet straight-backed.

dialogue.text: The Quarterly Review would later note the charge: that Shankar Shah and his son plotted against Europeans, stirring revolt with their songs; some later accounts question how strong the evidence truly was.

i18n.hi: क्वार्टरली रिव्यू ने बाद में अभियोग दर्ज किया: कि शंकर शाह और उसका बेटा यूरोपियों के ख़िलाफ़ षड्यंत्र रचते, गीतों से बग़ावत फूँकते; कुछ बाद की लिखतें इस सबूत को ही कमज़ोर बताती हैं।

panels.shot: medium shot inside a barrack-room or makeshift court, Shankar and Raghunath standing guarded before a table of British officers
panels.action: Inside a bare barrack room, Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah stand bound yet calm before a table of British officers, one reading from a paper as sepoy guards flank the prisoners.

dialogue.speaker: shankar_shah_and_raghunath_shah
dialogue.text: Our words praise our land; you hear them as war.

i18n.hi: हमारे बोल अपनी मिट्टी की बड़ाई करें, तुम उन्हें जंग समझ लेते हो।

panels.shot: tight close-up on Shankar’s lined face, eyes steady; behind him blurred British figures confer
panels.action: A close view captures the lined face of Shankar Shah, his eyes steady, as in the blurred background British officials lean together in quiet, tense discussion.

dialogue.text: In a season of revolt from Meerut to central India, authorities in Jabalpur chose severity. They read his poems as sedition, his Gond lineage as a threat, and they moved quickly to make an example.

i18n.hi: मेरठ से मध्य भारत तक उठती बग़ावत के मौसम में, जबलपुर हुक्मरानोंने सख़्ती चुनी। उन्होंने उसकी कविताओं को बग़ावत, गोंड वंश को ख़तरा पढ़ा, और मिसाल बनाने को जल्दी की।

panels.shot: wide shot of the Jabalpur parade ground at dawn, cannon lined up, sepoys formed, Shankar and Raghunath led in chains
panels.action: On the parade ground at dawn, British cannon stand in a row before assembled sepoys, as Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah are led in chains across the packed dirt.

dialogue.text: On 18 September 1857, the pensioned Gond descendant and his son were marched to the Jabalpur parade ground, the day chosen to display British power before troops and town.

i18n.hi: १८ सितम्बर १८५७ को, पेंशनख़ोर गोंड वंशज और उसका बेटा जबलपुर परेड मैदान पर लाए गए, वही दिन चुना गया ताकि फौज और शहर के सामने अंग्रेज़ी ताकत दिखे।

panels.shot: grim medium shot from the side as Shankar and Raghunath are bound in front of a cannon, ropes taut, sepoys watching
panels.action: A side view shows Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah being tightly bound in front of the mouth of a British cannon, sepoys watching in rigid silence as ropes pull against their chests and arms.

dialogue.text: Contemporary reports state plainly: they were blown from cannon, an execution method used in 1857 to punish those the British branded as rebels, to break bodies and send a public warning.

i18n.hi: समकालीन रिपोर्टें साफ़ लिखती हैं: उन्हें तोप के मुँह से उड़ाया गया, वही सज़ा जो १८५७ में उन पर दी जाती थी जिन्हें अंग्रेज़ बाग़ी ठहराते, ताकि देह तो टूटे ही, डर भी सब पर छा जाए।

panels.shot: close three-quarter shot on father and son bound together, faces turned slightly to each other, cannon looming behind
panels.action: Bound before the gun, Shankar Shah turns his head slightly toward Raghunath Shah, their faces close, the dark bore of the cannon just behind them and a ring of soldiers in the blur.

dialogue.speaker: shankar_shah_and_raghunath_shah
dialogue.text: Let them fear our words more than this iron.

i18n.hi: लोहे से नहीं, हमारी बातों से डरें।

panels.shot: tight on the cannon’s muzzle, the lanyard held by a sepoy’s trembling hand, faces of sepoys conflicted around
panels.action: The dark circle of the cannon's muzzle fills the foreground as a sepoy's hand grips the firing cord, his knuckles tight, other sepoys around him rigid, some unable to meet the sight ahead.

dialogue.text: Bayly and others have shown how, in such moments, colonial power relied on spectacle and fear, yet also risked unsettling the very sepoys on whose obedience that power stood.

i18n.hi: बेले जैसे इतिहासकार दिखाते हैं कि ऐसे मौकों पर औपनिवेशिक राज दिखावे और दहशत पर टिका था, पर इसी से उन सिपाहियों का दिल भी डगमगाने लगता था जिनकी वफ़ादारी पर वही राज टिका था।

panels.shot: wide shot a moment later, with drifting smoke obscuring the foreground; sepoy ranks visible through the haze
panels.action: A cloud of thick smoke bellows from the cannon line, veiling the foreground, while through the haze rigid sepoy ranks stand motionless, their faces barely visible.

dialogue.text: The British reports record the sentence carried out. Local tellings would later remember his last poem as rising above the thunder, even as his body did not survive the blast.

i18n.hi: अंग्रेज़ी रिपोर्टें फाँसला पूरा होना दर्ज करती हैं। लोककथाएँ कहती हैं, उसकी आख़िरी कविता तोप की गर्जना से ऊपर उठी, भले उसका जिस्म धमाके से मिट गया।

panels.shot: medium shot of sepoys of the 52nd Bengal Native Infantry murmuring among themselves by their barracks later, anger and unease on their faces
panels.action: By the barracks later, sepoys of the 52nd Bengal Native Infantry gather in small knots, their faces tight with anger and unease, hands gesturing as they speak in low, urgent tones.

dialogue.text: Within days, the 52nd Bengal Native Infantry mutinied at Jabalpur. Contemporary accounts link their fury in part to the execution, seeing in it a spark for anger already laid by wider grievances.

i18n.hi: कुछ ही दिनों में ५२वीं बंगाल नेटिव इंफ़ैन्ट्री ने जबलपुर में बग़ावत कर दी। समकालीन बयान मानते हैं कि उनकी तैश में इस फाँसी की चिंगारी भी थी, जो पहले से भड़की शिकायतों पर गिरी।

panels.shot: montage-like wide shot showing unrest across central India: small fires in villages, marching bands of rebels, British columns
panels.action: A montage across the central Indian landscape shows village fires in the distance, armed bands moving along jungle tracks, and British columns marching as monsoon clouds gather overhead.

dialogue.text: Eric Stokes would later trace how such local shocks joined larger currents: peasant discontent, sepoy fears, ruined chiefs and princes, all feeding into the fractured landscape of 1857.

i18n.hi: एरिक स्टोक्स ने दिखाया कि ऐसे स्थानीय झटके कैसे बड़ी धाराओं से जुड़ गए: किसानों की कुंठा, सिपाहियों की घबराहट, उजड़े राजा‑रजवाड़े, सब मिलकर १८५७ की टूटी‑फूटी ज़मीन को खुराक देते गए।

panels.shot: evocative shot of a village storyteller under a tree years later, with children and adults listening; ghostly image of Shankar and Raghunath suggested in the dusk sky
panels.action: Years later, a village storyteller sits under a spreading tree near Mandla, men and children listening as, in the dim evening sky above them, faint shapes suggest Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah side by side.

dialogue.text: In the Gond memoryscape of Garha-Mandla, he did not remain a failed pensioner, but became a figure of song again, his death folded into tales of the forest kings and their defiance.

i18n.hi: गरहा‑मंडला की गोंड स्मृतियों में वह नाकाम पेंशनभोगी नहीं रहा, फिर से गीतों का नायक बना, उसकी मौत जंगल के राजाओं और उनकी सरकशी की कथाओं में घुल गई।

panels.shot: final contemplative wide shot of the empty Jabalpur parade ground at sunset, with a lone cannon and long shadows, Shankar and Raghunath’s figures faintly superimposed
panels.action: At sunset the Jabalpur parade ground lies almost empty, a single cannon resting idle as long shadows stretch over the dirt, and faint, transparent figures of Shankar Shah and Raghunath Shah stand beyond it, facing the horizon.

dialogue.text: An empire tried to silence a pensioned prince by blowing his body from a gun, yet the story of Shankar Shah’s last poem endures as a reminder of how rulers fear not just rebellion, but remembering itself.

i18n.hi: एक साम्राज्य ने पेंशनख़ोर राजकुमार को तोप से उड़ा कर चुप कराने की सोची, पर शंकर शाह की आख़िरी कविता की कहानी आज भी याद दिलाती है कि हुक्मरान केवल बग़ावत से नहीं, याद से भी डरते हैं।

subtitle_i18n.en: A pensioned prince, a frightened empire, and a poem that would not die
subtitle_i18n.hi: पेंशन पर जीता राजकुमार, डरा हुआ साम्राज्य, और एक अमर कविता
